newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randfontein to shed third of workforce.
newsitem.headline: Randfontein to shed third of workforce.

text.p: JCI Ltd said on Wednesday its Randfontien Estates Gold Mining Co Ltd unit planned to shed around a third of its 12,000-strong workforce and cut tonnage throughput as part of a far-reaching restructuring at the struggling gold mine.

JCI said that the planned date for the retrenchments was May 31. "Agreement has been reached with most unions and associations on the terms of the reduction/retrenchment, and it is expected that the outstanding agreements will be concluded this week," the group said in a statement.

The workforce would be reduced by between 3,400 and 4,100 employees, JCI said. The reduction would be dependent upon the use of certain contractors and positions would be offered to retrenched workers on other JCI gold mines wherever possible.

"Management regrets the need to reduce the workforce by this large number of people, but this is essential in order to improve margins and efficiences and thereby enable the funding of new developments so as to ensure the future viability of the mine and the job security of the remaining employees," JCI said.
The announcement confirmed reports on Tuesday that the mine was considering retrenching up to two thirds of its workforce.

Randfontein produced 4,392 kg of gold in the March quarter compared to 5,100 kg in the December quarter. It plunged into a loss of 2.86 million rand, well down on the previous quarter's 43.83 million rand profit.
At the time of reporting the March quarter the mine announced that these results could lead to a further labour retructuring programme.
JCI said that as a result of the restructuring the tonnage throughput would be reduced to allow for more optimal mining of the orebody at an increased grade.
"It is imperative that the funding of the new South Reef section of Randfontein Estates is achieved through efficient and profitable oepration if the older section of the mine."
The group also urged that more shifts be worked.
"It is still necessary to address the fundamental obstacles impacting on the mine's optimal performance, such as an inability to work on Sundays and inflexible work practices."
JCI said the entire restructuring would take place with maximum consultation with all parties.
